title: The Burning Wolf Revisited
premise: Wren Vane has spent their whole life in Hollowmere, a valley warded against magic, hiding the beast-speech that lets them hear and command animals. When the crown's witch-hunters breach the valley's wards hunting gift-bearers, Wren flees into a world where their power marks them as both weapon and heresy. Guided by a disgraced huntress and a wolf who remembers the old covenant between human and wild magic, Wren learns that the thirteenth moon will seal the realms apart forever unless someone reforges the broken pact at the Moonstone Altar. Betrayed by an ally who wants the covenant dead, Wren must choose between erasing their gift to survive or embracing it fully—knowing either path may cost them everything—to renew the covenant and save both realms from unraveling.
about_author: Marguerite Joubert is the pen name of a former wildlife rehabilitator who spent a decade listening to what animals couldn't say aloud. She writes fantasy from a farmhouse in the hills, where she claims the local foxes offer editorial notes.

chapters.title: The Valley That Forgets
chapters.summary: Wren Vane's POV. Wren tends goats in Hollowmere, quietly using forbidden beast-speech to calm a sick ewe while hiding the gift even from family. A crow warns of strangers on the ridge. Emotional beat: the suffocating comfort of a life built on silence.

chapters.title: Iron in the Warding
chapters.summary: Wren's POV. Crown hunters arrive bearing iron charms that fray the valley's ancient wards; Wren watches from the treeline as they interrogate neighbors about 'gifted ones.' The wards flicker for the first time in generations. Emotional beat: dread—the invisible life is ending.

chapters.title: What the Foxes Knew
chapters.summary: Wren's POV. The foxes tell Wren the valley's ward was itself a covenant-seal, not natural protection, and it is dying. Wren's mother discovers the gift during a desperate night and begs Wren to run. Emotional beat: betrayal by safety; home becomes a trap.

chapters.title: Thirteen Moons
chapters.summary: Wren's POV. An old hedge-witch explains the covenant: thirteen moons until it fails entirely, severing wild magic and dooming gifted folk like Wren. Hunters close in; Wren flees over the ridge at dawn. Emotional beat: grief and the first taste of terrifying freedom.

chapters.title: The Wolf Who Remembers
chapters.summary: Wren's POV. In the deep forest Wren meets Ashfall, a great grey wolf who speaks—not through Wren's gift but independently—and claims to have sworn the original covenant. He offers guidance at a price: truthfulness. Emotional beat: wary wonder; Wren is no longer alone or in control.

chapters.title: A Huntress Disgraced
chapters.summary: Sera Kell's POV. Sera, a former royal huntress who refused to kill a gifted child, tracks Wren intending to warn, not capture. She saves Wren from a hunter patrol, earning distrust. Emotional beat: guilt seeking redemption through dangerous company.

chapters.title: Road of Ashes
chapters.summary: Alternating Wren/Sera POV. The trio passes villages burned by the purge; survivors whisper of a 'Moon Court' resistance. Wren uses beast-speech publicly for the first time to save a child, exposing themselves. Emotional beat: the cost of compassion in a hostile world.

chapters.title: The Gilded Cage
chapters.summary: Sera's POV. They shelter with Lord Aldric Vey, a charming noble who shelters gifted refugees—at a price: their service. Sera recognizes his collection of bound magical creatures and grows suspicious. Emotional beat: charm curdling into horror.

chapters.title: Voices in the Dark
chapters.summary: Wren's POV. At night Wren hears the caged creatures screaming in the old tongue; Ashfall urges escape, Sera counsels patience to learn Vey's plans. Wren secretly frees a wounded hawk. Emotional beat: moral awakening—silence is complicity.

chapters.title: The Moon Court
chapters.summary: Wren's POV. Vey reveals he leads the Moon Court resistance and wants Wren as its voice—but his plan is to seize the covenant's power, not restore it. Wren pretends allegiance while Ashfall teaches them the old rites. Emotional beat: seduction of power and purpose.

chapters.title: Lessons in Wild Tongues
chapters.summary: Wren's POV. Training montage among forest beings: Wren learns the covenant was a mutual vow, not domination, and that their gift's true form is listening, not commanding. Flashbacks to childhood. Emotional beat: identity reframed—strength as receptivity.

chapters.title: Sera's Confession
chapters.summary: Sera's POV. Sera admits she once led the raid that killed Wren's aunt, a gifted woman; she has been tracking redemption ever since. Wren's fury nearly shatters the alliance. Emotional beat: rage, then the hard arithmetic of forgiveness.

chapters.title: The Thirteenth Turn Begins
chapters.summary: Wren's POV. The final lunar cycle starts; the sky's moon shows a hairline crack, and wild magic begins failing—crops blight, beasts frenzy. Vey mobilizes the Moon Court toward the Moonstone Altar. Emotional beat: ticking clock made visible.

chapters.title: Betrayal at the Ford
chapters.summary: Alternating POV. Vey sells the group's location to crown hunters to eliminate rivals, and Sera is captured covering Wren's escape. Ashfall is gravely wounded. Emotional beat: devastation; every trust now suspect.

chapters.title: Alone Under a Cracking Sky
chapters.summary: Wren's POV. Wren nurses Ashfall in a cave, tempted to renounce the gift so hunters can't sense them—a false survival offered by a passing spirit. Wren refuses. Emotional beat: the dark night of the soul; choosing selfhood over safety.

chapters.title: The Prisoner of Greyhollow
chapters.summary: Sera's POV. In the hunter fortress, Sera bargains information for time, discovering the crown's true aim: harvest the covenant's power at the altar for the king. She escapes with a stolen map. Emotional beat: cunning as love's instrument.

chapters.title: Reunion of Strays
chapters.summary: Alternating POV. Sera finds Wren and Ashfall; forgiveness is tentative but real. Together they decode the rite: the covenant must be renewed freely by one who holds both human and wild blood-right—Wren alone qualifies. Emotional beat: fragile hope rekindled.

chapters.title: March of the Broken Moon
chapters.summary: Wren's POV. Racing the final moonrise, they gather unlikely allies—freed creatures, sympathetic villagers, even repentant hunters. Vey's forces and the crown converge on the altar. Emotional beat: found-family courage before the storm.

chapters.title: The Moonstone Altar
chapters.summary: Wren's POV. Climax begins: at the altar, Vey seizes the rite, demanding the covenant's power submit to him; the stone rejects him violently. Hunters attack; Sera duels the witch-finder general. Emotional beat: chaos where ambition meets something older than want.

chapters.title: What Wren Vane Chose
chapters.summary: Wren's POV. Climax resolves: mortally threatened, Wren speaks the covenant in the true tongue—not command but promise—offering their gift as bridge rather than blade. The moon mends; magic floods back balanced. Vey falls to his own seized power. Emotional beat: transcendence through surrender.

chapters.title: After the Thirteenth
chapters.summary: Sera's POV. Aftermath: the realms knit together; gifted folk emerge from hiding under a new accord brokered by Wren's example. Sera takes up guardianship of the altar roads. Emotional beat: quiet reckoning and earned peace.

chapters.title: Homecoming, Rewritten
chapters.summary: Wren's POV. Wren returns to Hollowmere, wards dissolved, and reconciles with their mother—no longer hidden, no longer the same. Ashfall departs into the wilds with a promise: listen, and I will answer. Emotional beat: belonging chosen, not inherited; the story closes on an open door.
